name: Opción a la Nacionalidad (Children of Transient/Diplomatic Foreign Parents Born in Chile)

qualifying_event.description: Chile's Constitution (Article 10) excludes from automatic birthright citizenship children born in Chile whose parents were either serving a foreign government in a diplomatic capacity, or were 'extranjeros transeúntes' (transient foreigners) at the time of birth. Such a person may nonetheless OPT into Chilean nationality within one year of turning 18.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Birth certificate/official birth record explicitly stating 'Hijo de Extranjero Transeúnte' or 'Hijo de extranjero que se encuentran en Chile al servicio de su gobierno'.

requirements.blocker_text: Birth certificate or official birth record explicitly notes 'Hijo de Extranjero Transeúnte' or diplomatic-service parentage.
Application must be submitted within 1 year of turning 18.

evidence_required.document: Letter to the National Director of SERMIG requesting the nationality option
Birth certificate/official birth record with the transeúnte or diplomatic-service notation

sources.title: tramites.extranjeria.gob.cl (Chile's official immigration procedures portal) -- Opción a la Nacionalidad: for children born in Chile to parents who were foreign diplomatic staff or 'extranjeros transeúntes' at the time of birth; application within 1 year of turning 18; cost CLP 37,979 (effective 1 May 2025); processed through tramites.serviciomigraciones.cl with ClaveÚnica

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Chile). Modeled PUBLISHED -- directly and fully tier-1 sourced. STRUCTURAL FINDING: Chile's constitutional citizenship regime is jus soli by default (birth in Chile generally confers citizenship), but Article 10 carves out an EXCEPTION for children of transient foreigners or foreign diplomatic staff -- OPPOSITE of most 'option' or exception routes elsewhere in this dataset, which typically grant a path INTO citizenship for children who would otherwise lack it (see Jordan's or Chad's narrower descent frameworks). Here, a child born in Chile under the exclusion is NOT automatically Chilean and must actively opt in as an adult -- effectively the mirror image of Botswana's or Jordan's descent files. Category is modeled as 'settled' rather than 'ancestry' since the route is not really about ancestry/heritage at all -- it hinges on birthplace and a parental-status technicality, closest in spirit to a status-regularisation route.
